description: The Office of Congressional Ethics (OCE), an independent, non-partisan investigative entity established by the United States House of Representatives, seeks one attorney with 5-10 years of experience to serve as Investigative Counsel. The Investigative Counsel reports to the Staff Director and Chief Counsel and will be responsible for conducting sensitive inquiries into allegations of possible violations of federal law and ethical standards of conduct by current Members, Officers and Staff of the House of Representatives and advising the Staff Director and Chief Counsel on legal and policy matters. The OCE is seeking attorneys interested in the OCE's work supporting ethics and transparency within the House of Representatives. The Investigative Counsel would join a small, Washington, DC-based, investigative team, and would be eligible to apply for hybrid work accommodations combining in-person core days and remote work.
responsibilities: Review information received by OCE, discern possible violations, and identify facts requiring further investigation
Plan, organize and conduct investigations regarding allegations and advise the Staff Director and Chief Counsel regarding appropriate evaluation of cases
Advise the Staff Director and Chief Counsel on legal issues in matters under investigation and on broader legal and policy issues involved in the operations of OCE
Draft lengthy and detailed memoranda, reports, and referrals for Board consideration and potential public release
Developing investigative strategies and implementing investigative plans
Reviewing evidence and data in order to analyze, develop, and provide detailed written and oral reports of findings
Identifying information to substantiate or disprove allegations and assess the likely sources of that information
Collecting and reviewing documents, electronic media, and physical evidence
Interviewing witnesses and subjects
Performing other duties as assigned
qualifications: 5-10 years of legal experience
Demonstrated ability to conduct and direct complex legal research and present the results in a clear, precise and persuasive manner
Thoroughness and careful attention to detail
Strong oral and written communication skills
Strong legal judgment and demonstrated professional integrity
Experience auditing large sets of data or evidence and providing detailed analysis
Investigative experience with high-profile and sensitive matters (desirable but not required)
Experience with investigations involving public officials (desirable but not required)
Experience with campaign finance or ethics law (desirable but not required)
Experience conducting interviews or depositions (desirable but not required)
Experience writing public reports or legal documents (desirable but not required)

Advanced proficiency in development and use of electronic databases, and other computer skills including knowledge of current information technology tools related to investigations (desirable but not required)
Ability to work independently or as part of an investigative team
Ability to manage multiple tasks and projects
Ability to work well under pressure and tight time deadlines
Ability to exercise discretion and independent judgment
Ability to pass Security Background Investigation to obtain Top Secret clearance
Graduation from an ABA accredited law school and active bar membership
how_to_apply: Please send cover letter, short writing sample, and resume (electronic submissions preferred) to Omar S. Ashmawy, Staff Director and Chief Counsel, Office of Congressional Ethics, United States House of Representatives, P.O. Box 895, Washington, DC 20515-0895, or OCEJOB@mail.house.gov.
